doc.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Where his perseverance comes from
summary: Wein cannot say why he kept going, and credits his wife Joyce's remark about his always thinking of something to do.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: How do you account for your just continuing on? We're talking about a time when you were still quite young, still before Newport, and it doesn't work, and you get disappointed, and somebody does you wrong, and yet you were steadfast.
Yes you are. Where does that come from?

I don't know. You don't know your own character. My wife Joyce said, "You know" …. She fell in love with me, which she did, thank god … she said, "When I realized that you are always thinking of something to do, that you are never sitting there without thinking of something to do." She respected that. I guess that that's … when I had nothing to do, I was thinking of something to do. That's the entrepreneurial spirit, I guess. I always tell someone, "If you want to be free and you want to have a chance in making money, go into business for yourself, because if you work for somebody else, there's this ceiling that you reach. If you go into business for yourself, you may lose everything you have, which I did several times, but you got a chance."
